assignment:
Some of your friends perform community service. For example, some tutor elementary school children and others clean up litter. They think helping the community is very important. But other friends of yours think community service takes too much time away from what they need or want to do. 
Your principal is deciding whether to require all students to perform community service. 
Write a letter to your principal in which you take a position on whether students should be required to perform community service. Support your position with examples.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about whether our school should make every student do community service. I do not think it should be a rule. I think the school should offer it and make it easy to join.

Some of my friends volunteer. One of them tutors third graders in reading after school. She says the kids get really excited when a hard word finally makes sense. Another friend joins a cleanup at the creek near our neighborhood on Saturdays. They both like it, and I can see why. Service teaches you to be patient and responsible. It also makes you feel part of something bigger.

But a requirement would be unfair to a lot of students. Many of us have full schedules. Some have part-time jobs to help pay the bills at home. Others watch their younger brothers and sisters, or they have practice for a team every day. My friend Marcus works at a grocery store four evenings a week. Making him find extra hours for service is a lot to ask, and his grades could drop.

Another thing is the reason people do it. When something is forced, most people do the minimum and watch the clock. A student who has to sign a log sheet might not care at all. Service that comes from your own choice means more to the student and to the people getting help. I have seen this happen with school clubs too.

Here is what I suggest instead of a rule. The school could hold a volunteer fair where local groups like food banks, libraries, and animal shelters explain what they need. We could do service projects during lunch or on school grounds, so students with busy days do not need extra travel. We could also give volunteers a certificate or a shout out at assemblies. When students see classmates getting honored, I think more of them will want to join. However, it has to be easy, or hardly anybody will sign up.

I believe this plan would get more students involved, and it would work better than a rule. Thank you for reading my opinion.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about whether our school should make every student do community service. I think it should not be required, but the school should encourage it and make it easy to do.

Some of my friends volunteer and they are proud of it. One helps third graders with reading after school, and she says their faces light up when a hard word finally makes sense. Another goes to a creek cleanup near our neighborhood on weekends. They both feel that helping others matters, and I agree. Service teaches you to be responsible and patient, and it shows you that you are part of something bigger than yourself.

However, a requirement would cause problems. Many students already have very full schedules. Some have part-time jobs to help their families pay bills. Others take care of their younger brothers and sisters or play on teams that practice every day. For them, a service quota would be one more thing on time they barely have. My friend works at a grocery store four nights a week. If you told him to find extra hours for service, it would stress him out and it could hurt his grades.

Another problem is the reason people do it. When something is forced, a lot of people do the bare minimum and watch the clock. A student who has to sign a log sheet might start to hate volunteering instead of liking it. Service that comes from your own choice usually means more, both to the student and to the people who get helped.

Instead of a requirement, I think the school should create more chances for students to help. We could have a volunteer fair where local groups like food banks, libraries, and animal shelters tell us what they need. We could also have service projects during lunch or on school grounds so busy students can join without traveling far. Another idea is to give volunteers certificates or say their names at assemblies. If students see their classmates having fun with service and getting honored for it, more of them will want to join too.

I believe this plan will get more students involved on their own, and with better attitudes, than a rule ever could. Thank you for reading my opinion.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
